feedback_correct: Correct. A commit records a snapshot of every tracked file as staged at that moment, not only the lines that changed since the previous commit.

feedback_by_distractor.B: This option treats a commit as recording only the lines that changed, but a commit stores a snapshot of every tracked file as it stood when staged.
feedback_by_distractor.C: This option treats a commit as storing a computed difference from the previous commit; `git diff` computes a difference between two snapshots on the spot, it does not read one Git stored directly.
feedback_by_distractor.D: This option treats an untouched file as left out of the new commit entirely, but a file you did not touch still refers to the same stored content as the previous commit, so it is still part of the snapshot.

feedback_correct: Correct. Merging integrates one branch's own work into another; whether that produces a new commit depends on whether history allows a fast-forward.

feedback_by_distractor.B: This option stages the file before its conflict markers are removed; Git does not block that commit by default, but the file still holds unresolved markers when committed, so the order matters.
feedback_by_distractor.C: This option assumes every merge must add a new commit; a fast-forward merge only moves the branch label forward, so no merge commit is created.
feedback_by_distractor.D: This option treats `git merge --abort` as finishing the merge, but it cancels the merge and returns to the state before it started, discarding any resolution already made, rather than completing it.
